question: Should OpenClaw make the new UX recovery bug-report dropdowns required in the public issue form, or collect the same context with optional/lighter fields?
rationale: The YAML change is mechanically correct, but the required-field choice affects contributor friction and issue-intake policy, which automation cannot safely decide for maintainers.

options.title: Accept current required dropdowns
options.body: Merge the PR as-is because the two required dropdowns are low-friction structured inputs that now feed the merged ClawSweeper UX release-blocker rubric.

options.title: Make recovery fields optional
options.body: Ask for the bug-report UX fields to be optional if maintainers want the signal without blocking reporters who lack that context.

options.title: Pause intake changes
options.body: Leave templates unchanged for now if maintainers want to observe the new ClawSweeper rubric before changing OpenClaw issue forms.

recommendation.title: Accept current required dropdowns
recommendation.body: Merge the PR as-is because the two required dropdowns are low-friction structured inputs that now feed the merged ClawSweeper UX release-blocker rubric.
